sstv_sideband_note: Band plans don't give a sideband. The sidebands follow the voice convention in the FCC General question pool (G2A01/G2A02): LSB on 160/75/40 m, USB at 14 MHz and up.

cw.note: CW-only or CW/narrow segments from the IARU Region 2 band plan (Sept 2020), kHz. The ARRL band plan page lists CW only for 160 m and 10 m (28.000-28.070 and 28.150-28.190) and 1.810 'CW QRP'. US law (47 CFR 97.305) allows CW anywhere in the amateur bands, so these segments are voluntary.

chu.status: off the air: NRC ended the CHU shortwave broadcasts on June 22, 2026

evidence.what: NRC 'Canada's official time' page now lists only the web clock, NTP, computer time codes and the telephone talking clock; no shortwave service
The NRC CHU page (nrc.canada.ca/.../nrc-shortwave-station-broadcasts-chu) returned 404 when fetched today. Its search-index snippet reads 'as of June 22, 2026 ... no longer be available'.
A reader comment on swling.com quotes an NRC technical officer: shutdown June 22, 10:00-10:30 EDT

chu.note: Keep CHU out of the active directory. If it's kept as a historical entry, the frequencies were not confirmed on a fetched NRC page (see unverified).

navtex_hf.confirmed: 47 CFR 80.1135(e): 'Internationally, the frequency 4209.5 kHz is used for NAVTEX-type transmissions by means of narrow-band direct-printing telegraphy with forward error correction'. 518 kHz is the international NAVTEX frequency and 490 kHz is the national/second-language one (80.1135(c),(d)).
navtex_hf.finding: No station near Connecticut was found using 4209.5 kHz. The Canadian Coast Guard's Radio Aids to Marine Navigation 2026 (Part 2) lists Atlantic NAVTEX only on 518 kHz (English) and 490 kHz (French). Those stations are Yarmouth U/V, Port Caledonia (Sydney) Q/J, Moisie C/D, Cartwright X, Robin Hood Bay O and Iqaluit T/S. The only HF MSI in RAMN is 8416.5 kHz NBDP from Iqaluit. The US NAVTEX list (USCG NAVCEN) returned 403, so US stations weren't checked directly.

unverified.why: These are HFGCS voice (USB) frequencies in hobbyist and Wikipedia lists, not ALE. The only official page (ACC fact sheet, acc.af.mil) returned 403, and the af.mil search results had no frequency list. HFGCS ALE frequencies (e.g. 11226, 9025, 13215 and others in hobbyist logs) have no public primary source. Leave all HFGCS entries out of the ALE list. If voice entries are added, label them hobbyist-sourced.
No USCG or DHS source publishes these. Only hobbyist logs exist (udxf.nl, ominous-valve, RadioReference), and they disagree (e.g. 8912 vs 8983).
Army/Air Force MARS don't publish a standing ALE channel list publicly. ARRL points to the Army MARS site for Armed Forces Day test frequencies only, and that wasn't fetched. Hobbyist lists only.

WSJT-X's default frequency list has no 60 m WSPR entry, and its user guide only says to choose a 60 m frequency that meets local rules. Neither number was found on wsprnet.org or in WSJT-X docs; only blogs mention them. Note that 5.3647 USB puts the signal at about 5.3661-5.3663 MHz, inside the US 5351.5-5366.5 kHz segment. 5.2872 is outside every US channel, so US stations can't transmit there.

Not on the Feld Hell Club list, which gives 14.063 (preferred, up to 14.069) and 14.072-14.073 on 20 m. 3.582, 7.082 and 10.142 fall inside the club's ranges, but the club lists ranges, not those exact spots.
